questions.qText: When a solid is heated and begins to melt, the temperature remains constant until all the solid has turned into a liquid. What is the heat energy being used for during this time?
options: Breaking the strong covalent bonds between the atoms.
Overcoming the attractive forces between the particles.
Increasing the kinetic energy of the particles.
Expanding the physical volume of the particles.

questions.qText: Carbon dioxide gas is pressurised and cooled to form liquid carbon dioxide for underground storage. How do the arrangement and movement of the molecules change during this physical process?
options: Particles move closer and vibrate in fixed positions.
Particles move further apart and vibrate in fixed positions.
Particles move closer together and slide past one another.
Particles move further apart and move randomly at high speeds.

questions.qText: Ammonia gas is less dense than air and highly soluble in water. Which method is most suitable for collecting a sample of ammonia gas in the laboratory?
options: Upward delivery into an inverted gas jar.
Downward delivery into an upright gas jar.
Downward displacement of water in a trough.
Bubbling the gas through a neutral salt solution.

questions.qText: Chlorine gas is denser than air and slightly soluble in water. How should a sample of chlorine gas be collected?
options: Upward delivery into an inverted gas jar.
Downward displacement of water in a trough.
Bubbling the gas through a neutral salt solution.
Downward delivery into an upright gas jar.

questions.qText: Hydrogen gas is insoluble in water and is the least dense gas. Which combination of methods can be used to collect it?
options: Upward delivery or downward displacement of water.
Downward delivery or upward displacement of water.
Upward delivery or upward displacement of water.
Downward delivery or downward displacement of water.

questions.qText: A student collects a colourless gas in a test tube. Which test and result confirms the gas is oxygen?
options: It bleaches damp litmus paper.
It relights a glowing splint.
It produces a white precipitate with limewater.
It makes a popping sound with a lighted splint.

questions.qText: Chlorine exists as two main isotopes: Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37. Which statement correctly defines why they are isotopes?
options: Same number of protons and neutrons.
Different number of protons, same neutrons.
Same number of protons, different neutrons.
Different number of protons and neutrons.

questions.qText: Which of the following ions has the exact same electronic configuration as an Argon atom (2,8,8)?
options: Sodium ion (Na+)
Magnesium ion (Mg2+)
Oxide ion (O2-)
Chloride ion (Cl-)

questions.qText: An ion X2+ contains 18 electrons and 20 neutrons. What is the nucleon number of element X?
Why is the relative atomic mass (Ar) of copper 63.5, rather than a whole number?
options: The weighted average mass of its naturally occurring isotopes.
The mass of a single atom compared to a hydrogen atom.
The total number of protons and neutrons in its heaviest isotope.
The average mass of its atoms minus the mass of its electrons.

questions.qText: When a sodium atom (Na) forms a sodium ion (Na+), what happens to its size and why?
options: It increases because it gains an extra electron shell.
It decreases because it loses its outermost electron shell.
It increases because the protons repel each other strongly.
It remains the same because the nucleus does not change.

questions.qText: An atom of phosphorus has a proton number of 15 and a nucleon number of 31. What is the number of protons, neutrons, and electrons in a phosphide ion (P3-)?
options: 15 protons, 16 neutrons, 18 electrons.
15 protons, 16 neutrons, 15 electrons.
15 protons, 31 neutrons, 18 electrons.
12 protons, 16 neutrons, 18 electrons.

questions.qText: Aluminium sulfate has the chemical formula Al2(SO4)3. Aluminium forms an Al3+ ion. What is the formula of the sulfate ion?
options: SO4-
SO4 2-
SO4 3-
SO4 4-

questions.qText: Iron(III) chloride has the chemical formula FeCl3. Chlorine is in Group 17 and forms a Cl- ion. What is the formula of the iron ion in this compound?
options: Fe+
Fe2+
Fe3+
Fe4+

questions.qText: Element P is in Group 2 of the Periodic Table and Element Q is in Group 17. What is the most likely formula of the ionic compound they form?
options: PQ
P2Q
PQ2
P2Q7

questions.qText: Why do ionic compounds like magnesium oxide have very high melting points?
options: Strong covalent bonds between atoms require high energy to break.
Weak intermolecular forces hold molecules together in a lattice.
Mobile delocalised electrons bind the ions tightly in a giant structure.
Strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions require high energy.

questions.qText: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity, but aqueous sodium chloride does. Which statement best explains this?
options: Solid does not conduct, aqueous does, because ions are free to move in solution.
Solid conducts, aqueous does not, because ions are fixed in the solid.
Solid conducts, aqueous does not, because water blocks the flow of electrons.
Solid does not conduct, aqueous does, because water provides the necessary electrons.

questions.qText: Ionic compounds are typically brittle. What happens at the particle level when a strong force is applied to an ionic crystal?
options: The covalent bonds snap under pressure, shattering the crystal into pieces.
Electrons are squeezed out of the lattice, causing the structure to collapse.
Layers of ions slide, bringing like charges together which repel and split the crystal.
The ions are compressed into a smaller volume, causing them to explode outwards.

questions.qText: Water (H2O) has a relatively low boiling point of 100 degrees Celsius. Which statement best explains this?
options: The covalent bonds between the atoms are weak and easily broken by heat.
The molecules are small and do not contain many electrons to share.
Simple molecular compounds have no forces of attraction between their atoms.
The intermolecular forces between the molecules are weak and easily overcome.

questions.qText: Why does liquid hydrogen chloride (HCl) not conduct electricity?
options: The covalent bonds are too strong to allow electrons to move freely.
It contains no mobile ions or free electrons to carry an electrical charge.
It only conducts when dissolved in water because water acts as a catalyst.
The molecules are too far apart in the liquid state to transfer electrons.

questions.qText: How many shared pairs of electrons are present in a single molecule of methane (CH4)?
The halogens (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) are all simple molecular covalent substances. Why does the boiling point increase as you go down Group 17 from fluorine to iodine?
options: The covalent bonds between the halogen atoms become stronger down the group.
The atoms become heavier, making them much harder to boil at higher temperatures.
The number of shared electron pairs increases significantly down the group.
The molecules become larger, leading to stronger intermolecular forces of attraction.

questions.qText: Which of the following molecules contains exactly two shared pairs of electrons (a double bond)?
options: Ammonia (NH3)
Water (H2O)
Oxygen (O2)
Chlorine (Cl2)

questions.qText: In a molecule of ammonia (NH3), how many lone pairs of electrons are present on the central nitrogen atom?
